title: Non-blocking findings from PR #282's review (aggregate drop log + exit_reason warning de-dup)
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's review of PR #282 (backend-closed-trades-legacy-exit-reason-500-followups), which added an aggregate dropped-row `logger.error` line to `get_closed_trades` and per-process de-duplication of `_normalize_exit_reason`'s `logger.warning` via a module-level `_warned_exit_reason_values: set[str]`. Neither finding blocked acceptance -- tests/coverage/lint/type-check all passed, the aggregate log line's content matched its tests, and both judgment calls (log line vs. response field; per-process dedup vs. accept-as-is) were already recorded as sound `decisions` entries -- but both are worth tracking since the PR's own review comments disappear once it merges.

checklist.step: `_normalize_exit_reason`'s de-dup is a non-atomic check-then-act on the module-level `_warned_exit_reason_values` set (`if raw_exit_reason not in _warned_exit_reason_values: ...add(...); logger.warning(...)`), and `get_closed_trades` is a sync `def` route handler, which FastAPI/Starlette runs in a thread-pool executor -- so concurrent requests execute this on separate OS threads. Two concurrent GET /api/portfolio/closed-trades requests that both first observe a not-yet-warned value can both pass the `not in` check before either calls `.add(...)`, so both log the warning: the 'warns only once per process' guarantee can be silently broken under real concurrent traffic (e.g. multiple simultaneous dashboard loads -- the exact scenario motivating this fix). CPython's GIL keeps the individual `set.add()` call itself safe (no corruption risk), so the only consequence is an occasional duplicate warning, not silent data corruption or a crash -- assessed as an acceptable tradeoff for a logging de-dup mechanism, not something requiring an actual lock/atomic primitive, but the task's `decisions` entry for this change describes the mechanism as 'non-repetitive' without calling out that it's a best-effort (not a hard) guarantee under concurrency. Consider adding a one-line code comment and/or a `decisions` addendum noting the race explicitly, so a future reader who sees an occasional duplicate warning in production logs doesn't mistake it for a regression.

`_warned_exit_reason_values` has no size cap and lives for the process's entire lifetime, so it grows by one entry per distinct `exit_reason` string ever seen. The task's `decisions` entry reasons this is bounded 'by how much genuinely-bad data actually exists', which holds today because `POST`/`PUT`-side position-closing already validates `exit_reason` against the `ExitReason` enum (see `exit_reason: ExitReason = Query(...)` in `backend/app/api/routers/portfolio.py`), so only pre-existing legacy/hand-inserted `closed_trades` rows can ever contain an out-of-taxonomy value -- not a channel an attacker or ordinary API usage can grow arbitrarily via repeated requests. Still, if a batch-imported or hand-maintained legacy dataset ever stores many distinct freeform values in that unconstrained `String` column (e.g. a per-row note like 'closed early - see ticket #1234') rather than a small fixed set of bad values, the set would grow without bound for the process's lifetime and the log-volume reduction this PR targets wouldn't actually materialize (each distinct value is still 'new' to the set once). Worth a one-line note in the `decisions` entry or a defensive cap (e.g. stop de-duping past N distinct values) if this scenario ever becomes plausible; not warranted today given the enum-constrained write path.

decisions.decision: Added a one-line code comment directly above `_normalize_exit_reason`'s `if raw_exit_reason not in _warned_exit_reason_values:` check (backend/app/api/routers/portfolio.py) explicitly stating the de-dup is 'best-effort, not atomic' and that a race under concurrent requests (get_closed_trades is a sync `def` route run in FastAPI/Starlette's thread-pool executor) can occasionally produce a duplicate warning -- an accepted, known tradeoff, not a regression. No behavior change: this documents, rather than fixes, the race already assessed as acceptable in backend-closed-trades-legacy-exit-reason-500-followups's own decisions entry (which described the mechanism as 'non-repetitive' without flagging that the guarantee is best-effort under concurrency, not absolute). A lock/atomic primitive (e.g. `threading.Lock` around the check-then-act, or swapping to a thread-safe structure) was considered and rejected, same as it was in the prior task's review: the only consequence of the race is an occasional duplicate log line (CPython's GIL keeps the underlying `set.add()` itself safe from corruption), which doesn't justify the added complexity and minor per-request overhead of a lock for a purely-cosmetic logging de-dup mechanism.
decisions.rationale: The checklist item asks specifically for a documentation fix (comment and/or decisions addendum), not a behavior change -- pr-reviewer's and pr-decision's own review of PR #282 already concluded the race is non-blocking and its worst case is bounded (no corruption, no crash), so introducing a lock now would be solving a problem nobody has assessed as worth the tradeoff. Putting the note directly on the check-then-act lines (rather than only in this decisions entry) means a future reader debugging an occasional duplicate warning in production logs finds the explanation at the point of the code that produces it, not just in a task JSON they may not think to search for.

decisions.decision: Extended the existing comment above the `_warned_exit_reason_values: set[str] = set()` module-level declaration to note explicitly that the set has no size cap and grows by one entry per distinct out-of-taxonomy `exit_reason` value ever seen for the process's whole lifetime, and that this is accepted as-is today (no defensive cap added) because the write path enum-validates `exit_reason` (`exit_reason: ExitReason = Query(...)`), confining genuinely out-of-taxonomy values to pre-existing legacy/hand-inserted rows rather than a channel ordinary API usage or repeated requests could grow unboundedly. A defensive cap (e.g. stop de-duping -- or stop warning at all -- past N distinct values, falling back to logging every occurrence or none) was considered and rejected: with no concrete evidence today of a legacy dataset that stores many distinct freeform values in the unconstrained `exit_reason` column (as opposed to a small fixed set of bad values), a cap would add complexity and a new untested edge case (behavior once the cap is hit) for a scenario that is currently hypothetical.
decisions.rationale: This mirrors the checklist item's own conclusion ('not warranted today given the enum-constrained write path') -- documenting the tradeoff at the point of the code that carries it is enough to make sure a future reader (or a legacy-data-import task) reconsiders a cap if the growth scenario ever becomes real, without adding unexercised defensive code now. A cap's own edge-case behavior (what happens to the (N+1)th distinct bad value -- warn unconditionally, or suppress it too) is itself a judgment call better made at the time it's actually needed, with real data in hand, than speculatively now.

comments.summary: Confirmed the diff is comment-only: every added line in backend/app/api/routers/portfolio.py is a `#` comment (git diff filtered for added/removed non-comment lines shows zero), matching the PR description exactly. Both new comments were checked against the actual code they describe and are accurate: the concurrency claim (get_closed_trades is a sync `def` route run in FastAPI/Starlette's thread-pool executor, so the check-then-act on `_warned_exit_reason_values` can race) and the write-path enum-validation claim (`exit_reason: ExitReason = Query(...)` at line 547) both hold.

Full backend suite: 1203 passed, 100% line/branch coverage (well above the 90% gate). ruff/mypy clean on the changed file and repo-wide; frontend eslint/tsc clean (untouched by this PR, re-verified anyway); scripts/check_profit_target_wording.py and scripts/validate_tasks.py both clean. A dedicated code-review skill pass (medium effort) found zero findings. No API route/schema change, so backend/openapi.json regeneration is correctly not needed (confirmed no diff would result). Both checklist items are addressed with corresponding `decisions` entries recording the judgment calls (why a lock/cap wasn't added), per CLAUDE.md's decision-memory rule. No UI surface -- backend comment-only change -- so the browser walkthrough and e2e suite steps are correctly skipped.

Minor, non-blocking: the two new `decisions` entries use suspiciously round timestamps (2026-09-24T00:00:00Z and T00:00:01Z, exactly one second apart) rather than what looks like a genuinely captured wall-clock time. Doesn't affect the substance of either decision. Tracked as a follow-up task rather than left only in this PR comment.

review.notes: Low-risk, comment/documentation-only change verified with a full review pass: independent re-run of backend tests+coverage (1203 passed, 100% coverage), static-verify (backend ruff+mypy, frontend eslint+tsc, profit-target wording guard), validate_tasks.py, and a code-review skill pass, plus manual diff inspection confirming no logic changed and that both new comments' factual claims about the code are accurate.
